data.narrative:
Orbit Fab, a Series A space and aerospace company, has raised $28.5M to date. The valuation universe comprises 6 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs, though the narrow peer set limits precision.

Only the stage-progression method is applicable here. Using total capital raised as a valuation proxy, the analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the next funding stage, yielding $57M. This reflects the progression assumption that capital deployed by Series A investors implies a post-round valuation approximately double the cumulative raise. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures, which private companies rarely disclose. Peer-median triangulation was not viable; while 14 same-sector peers exist, filtering for stage-appropriate and similar-tier comparables yielded fewer than 3 datapoints.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $48M to $66M, with a median point estimate of $57M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty. Key risks to the range include: absence of revenue-based validation, sparse early-stage comparable data in the space sector, and reliance on stage-progression multipliers that may not reflect Orbit Fab's specific unit economics or market position. Independent verification through management guidance, burn rate analysis, or customer traction data would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
